proof: NativeGroundDecalUniforms is 368 bytes; the standard-layout/trivially-copyable G02 aggregate places indices exactly at offset 368. The logical upload is 440 bytes; Buffer copies that length, excluding the host structure's 448-byte tail padding. Direct aggregate initialization preserves the 368-byte uniform prefix and initializes the exact existing 36 UInt16 words (NativeGroundDecalUploadPolicyG02.h:9-24; Metal4GroundDecal.mm:183-189).

The packed validity predicate checks nonzero 16-byte-aligned base address, actual length >=440, and full-range overflow before adding 368. The encoder binds the uniform at the original base and uses base+368 only for packed indices, with indexCount36, UInt16 type, indexBufferLength72, baseVertex0 and baseInstance0. The installed MTL4 SDK declaration accepts these units and alignment (NativeGroundDecalUploadPolicyG02.h:25-32; Metal4GroundDecal.mm:72-85; MTL4RenderCommandEncoder.h:383-425).

G02 is exact-string-1 opt-in and also requires the existing G01 eligibility. When G02 is off, G01 is off, sampleCount differs from one, or instances are empty, the original uniform upload and applicable old draw/index path remain. No shader, fragment, pipeline, world renderer or runtime change is present (Metal4GroundDecal.mm:169-205).

Optional packed newBufferWithBytes returning nil or an invalid tail resumes mandatory 368-byte uniform Buffer followed by the existing optional G01 72-byte index Buffer, all before Encode. Buffer/AddAllocation, mandatory uniform and argument-table exceptions are not caught or converted into a fallback. A failed optional allocation does not publish an index address (Metal4GroundDecal.mm:16,183-208).

A successful packed buffer is held strongly by the prepared packet as indicesG01 and once by the existing RuntimeLease::AddAllocation; the uniform argument table points into the same immutable object. Existing event/feedback retirement or failure quarantine owns the allocation through the frame, with no new reuse token or cross-frame owner (Metal4GroundDecal.mm:38-46,183-208; Metal4RuntimeNative.mm:769-782,1154-1196; Metal4WorldRenderer.mm:5783-5807).

The PROBE path counts successful uniform/index Buffer calls, records same-object identity and offset, and now has three atomic one-shot categories: packed indexed, separate indexed, nonindexed. Clean PROBE=0 bypasses counter writes, atomics and LOG (Metal4GroundDecal.mm:89-99,173-180,207).
